## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: SR-1 versus SR-22, investigated versus uninvestigated crashes, suspension versus revocation, three versus seven years, careless versus reckless driving, plus continuation facts on lapses, crash duties, demerit points and the online driver record
Confusable pairs among the insurance and driving-record rules, followed by continuation facts that did not fit part C; each block ties to one handbook page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec11-R01 | anchor: A01
Nevada law sets minimum liability insurance amounts that apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle in the state. [A01]
Why it matters: group insurance; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-R02 | anchor: A01
A police-investigated crash reaches the DMV through the officer's report, while a crash without police investigation that injures anyone or causes $750 or more in damage needs your own SR-1 within 10 days. [A01]
Why it matters: group crash reporting; confusable investigated versus uninvestigated.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-R03 | anchor: A01
Lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered. [A01]
Why it matters: group insurance lapses; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec11-R04 | anchor: A02
The SR-1 is a crash report you file, while the SR-22 is proof-of-insurance coverage that the DMV monitors when reinstating a suspended or revoked driver. [A02]
Why it matters: group forms; confusable SR-1 versus SR-22.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R05 | anchor: A02
The price of SR-22 coverage depends on how the insurance company structures it. [A02]
Why it matters: group forms; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R06 | anchor: A02
If a crash involves injuries, the first duties are to stop, get medical help and warn traffic; the move-it-aside rule covers a fender bender with property damage only and a vehicle that can be moved safely. [A02]
Why it matters: group crash scene; confusable injury crash versus fender bender.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec11-R07 | anchor: A03
Most violations stay reportable to insurers for three years, while DUI-related convictions stay on the record for seven years. [A03]
Why it matters: group driving record; confusable three versus seven years.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R08 | anchor: A03
Points-based suspension comes from reaching 12 points within 12 months, while revocation follows a single major conviction such as DUI that carries no points at all. [A03]
Why it matters: group driving record; confusable suspension versus revocation.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R09 | anchor: A03
Points from traffic school are removed only when the school reports your completion for credit, and the DMV will notify you if unsafe driving puts your license status in jeopardy. [A03]
Why it matters: group driving record; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec11-R10 | anchor: A04
Reckless driving carries 8 demerit points while careless driving carries 6. [A04]
Why it matters: group points; confusable reckless versus careless.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R11 | anchor: A04
A prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions costs 2 points, the same as speeding 11 to 20 mph over the limit. [A04]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R12 | anchor: A04
The point list is only partial, and holders of a commercial driver license may face extra penalties and points for some violations. [A04]
Why it matters: group points; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]

FACT_ID: sec11-R13 | anchor: A04
A free online account through the DMV website shows license status and expiration, a driver history printout, and full lists of demerit points, violation codes and court details. [A04]
Why it matters: group driving record; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0078]
